{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "PARTIALLY FEASIBLE — core question NOT answerable in single-column ELM; provide vertical proxy diagnostics only",
    "answerable": [
      "Vertical soil moisture, recharge, and drainage dynamics at individual representative hillslope positions (upland, mid-slope, toeslope/riparian)",
      "Column-local subsurface (baseflow) drainage flux (QDRAI) that feeds lateral flow, usable as a boundary input to an external routing/travel-time model",
      "Position-dependent water-table depth and saturated fraction that condition lateral exchange gradients",
      "PFLOTRAN 1D vertical Richards/Darcy transport to estimate local vertical residence times within each column"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Hillslope-to-stream travel TIMES — requires lateral flow routing along topographic flowpaths, which single-column ELM does not simulate",
      "Lateral flow CONVERGENCE along topographic flowpaths — needs multi-column topographic connectivity / a distributed or hillslope-connected model",
      "Groundwater EXCHANGE between neighboring hillslope positions — inter-column lateral saturated flow is disabled in single-column (each column is a closed vertical 1D domain)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "Three columns represent an idealized upland–midslope–toeslope catena along a Naches hillslope. Single-column ELM cannot pass water laterally between them, but running the three positions independently supplies the position-specific vertical fluxes (QDRAI, water-table depth, saturated fraction) that an external topographic routing / travel-time model (e.g., ELM hillslope-hydro coupled to MOSART, or PFLOTRAN 2D transects) would require as forcing. Fewer would not span the topographic gradient; more adds little without lateral coupling.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "naches_upland_ridge", "lat": 46.92, "lon": -121.05, "soil_texture": "gravelly sandy loam (thin, well-drained ridge soil)"},
    {"id": "naches_midslope", "lat": 46.88, "lon": -120.95, "soil_texture": "sandy loam (colluvial midslope)"},
    {"id": "naches_toeslope_riparian", "lat": 46.85, "lon": -120.88, "soil_texture": "silty clay loam (saturated riparian toeslope)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",
    "STOP_N": "15",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2000-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI", "QDRAI_PERCH", "QOVER", "QRUNOFF", "QRECHARGE",
      "ZWT", "ZWT_PERCH", "WA", "FSAT", "H2OSOI", "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE",
      "QINFL", "RAIN", "SNOW", "QFLX_SNOW_DRAIN", "TWS", "WT"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM_HILLSLOPE_HYDROLOGY (multi-column topographic unit with lateral saturated/subsurface exchange) — REQUIRED for the actual travel-time and convergence question; NOT available in standard single-column mode",
    "River/hillslope routing (MOSART or a 1D kinematic-wave flowpath router) to convert lateral fluxes into travel times",
    "PFLOTRAN 2D/3D transect coupling for explicit groundwater exchange and particle/tracer travel-time estimation"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Single-column ELM treats each column as an isolated 1D vertical domain; the requested lateral/convergence physics is therefore emulated only as independent point diagnostics, not solved.",
    "GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing (2000–2014) is representative of recent Naches climate; a spin-up (>=200 yr accelerated + transient) is run before the analysis window to equilibrate water table.",
    "Column locations and soil textures approximate an idealized ridge-to-riparian catena in the Naches River basin, WA (~46.9N, -121.0W).",
    "Deriving actual hillslope-to-stream travel times requires exporting QDRAI/ZWT to an external routing or PFLOTRAN model; single-column output alone yields only local vertical residence proxies."
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: PARTIALLY FEASIBLE — core question NOT answerable in single-column ELM; provide vertical proxy diagnostics only
answerable: Vertical soil moisture, recharge, and drainage dynamics at individual representative hillslope positions (upland, mid-slope, toeslope/riparian)
Column-local subsurface (baseflow) drainage flux (QDRAI) that feeds lateral flow, usable as a boundary input to an external routing/travel-time model
Position-dependent water-table depth and saturated fraction that condition lateral exchange gradients
PFLOTRAN 1D vertical Richards/Darcy transport to estimate local vertical residence times within each column
not_answerable: Hillslope-to-stream travel TIMES — requires lateral flow routing along topographic flowpaths, which single-column ELM does not simulate
Lateral flow CONVERGENCE along topographic flowpaths — needs multi-column topographic connectivity / a distributed or hillslope-connected model
Groundwater EXCHANGE between neighboring hillslope positions — inter-column lateral saturated flow is disabled in single-column (each column is a closed vertical 1D domain)

parsed.n_justification: Three columns represent an idealized upland–midslope–toeslope catena along a Naches hillslope. Single-column ELM cannot pass water laterally between them, but running the three positions independently supplies the position-specific vertical fluxes (QDRAI, water-table depth, saturated fraction) that an external topographic routing / travel-time model (e.g., ELM hillslope-hydro coupled to MOSART, or PFLOTRAN 2D transects) would require as forcing. Fewer would not span the topographic gradient; more adds little without lateral coupling.

columns.soil_texture: gravelly sandy loam (thin, well-drained ridge soil)

requires_capabilities: ELM_HILLSLOPE_HYDROLOGY (multi-column topographic unit with lateral saturated/subsurface exchange) — REQUIRED for the actual travel-time and convergence question; NOT available in standard single-column mode
River/hillslope routing (MOSART or a 1D kinematic-wave flowpath router) to convert lateral fluxes into travel times
PFLOTRAN 2D/3D transect coupling for explicit groundwater exchange and particle/tracer travel-time estimation
assumptions: Single-column ELM treats each column as an isolated 1D vertical domain; the requested lateral/convergence physics is therefore emulated only as independent point diagnostics, not solved.
GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing (2000–2014) is representative of recent Naches climate; a spin-up (>=200 yr accelerated + transient) is run before the analysis window to equilibrate water table.
Column locations and soil textures approximate an idealized ridge-to-riparian catena in the Naches River basin, WA (~46.9N, -121.0W).
Deriving actual hillslope-to-stream travel times requires exporting QDRAI/ZWT to an external routing or PFLOTRAN model; single-column output alone yields only local vertical residence proxies.
